markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Users favor coherent recent activity; explicit recency conditioning could reduce recommendations driven by older interests. This targets current-purpose mismatch and revival of stale preferences. (2) Electronics has the weakest sampled discrimination: 9.7% wrong-rank positions and a 0.0265 tenth-percentile margin. These motivate harder training comparisons, but do not establish validation ranking quality. (3) Collapse scores near 0.5 imply approximately orthogonal embeddings on average. Global embedding diversification therefore lacks diagnostic support.

**Related-work insights.** (1) [GRU4Rec BPR-max](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf) emphasizes high-scoring negatives, making it a direct response to weak separation. (2) [Hard-BPR](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.19276) motivates caution about false negatives; aggressive mining can penalize plausible future choices. (3) [2Gated-TimeGRU](https://aisel.aisnet.org/hicss-57/da/data_science/10/) supports elapsed-time conditioning within recurrence. Its reported results do not establish gains on this benchmark.

### Framework and candidate assessment

Three directions organize the evidence: temporal intent retention, candidate discrimination, and item identity. They operate respectively on recurrent state, training loss, and item representation.

Scores are originality / future potential / user alignment / model alignment / implementation difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| BPR-max with moderate negative pools | 2/7/4/9/2 | Directly targets confusing comparisons | Does not explicitly distinguish current from stale intent |
| Learned elapsed-time decay inside GRU | 4/7/8/5/4 | Discounts temporally distant interests | Time gaps do not identify purpose changes reliably |
| Joint title-token and ID embeddings | 4/7/7/6/6 | Shares artist/product identity signals | Lexical similarity can reinforce broad matches |
| **Time-decayed GRU with BPR-max** | **4/8/8/8/5** | Combines current-intent retention with competitor discrimination | Two mechanisms require separate ablations |

### Selected experiment

At 0% progress, test a small, jointly trained extension of the corrected GRU4Rec. Before each real interaction, decay the previous recurrent state using a bounded transformation of the observed inter-event gap; then apply the GRU update. Train with BPR-max over a moderate uniform negative pool, excluding known training positives.

This explicitly targets two user failures: older interests resurfacing and unrelated-purpose recommendations displacing recent-intent matches. Neither compatibility nor redundancy is directly observed, so improvements there remain unsupported. BPR-max addresses the measured Electronics separation weakness.

```text
for each real historical event:
    gap = elapsed time since previous real event
    retained = hidden * exp(-softplus(rate) * bounded_log_gap(gap))
    hidden = GRU(item_embedding(event), retained)
score positive and eligible sampled negatives
minimize BPR-max plus negative-score regularization
```

Use one checkpoint per category, seeds 0/42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch. Preserve routing and DATA_DIR. Padding must leave state unchanged; read the final nonpadding position. Update predictor writing and diagnostic compatibility together. Select exclusively through pinned macro validation HR@10; report sampled margins separately. Compare baseline, decay-only, BPR-max-only, and the combined model within the shared budget.

idea.description: A single GRU4Rec network per category with jointly learned elapsed-time decay of recurrent state and a BPR-max training objective over moderately sized negative pools.
idea.motivation: Temporal retention targets stale-interest revival and mismatch with recent coherent activity. BPR-max targets weak positive-negative discrimination, particularly Electronics' measured 9.7% wrong-rank rate. These are hypotheses requiring fixed validation evaluation.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain the corrected baseline's data loading, splits, routing, preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Use only historical timestamps, with zero gap for the first real event. Fit any gap normalization on training histories only. Apply decay only at real events and preserve hidden state through left padding. Maintain log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items); timestamp lookup or optional temporal inputs must preserve existing callers and use identical train/predict behavior. Read the final nonpadding position, never count-1. Exclude known training positives and the current positive from negative sampling without consulting held-out labels. Compute BPR-max using numerically stable log-softmax and logsigmoid operations. Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis); return measured metrics and definitions and omit unsupported metadata breakdowns. Embed the exact trained architecture and temporal preprocessing in the predictor writer. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint. Run sequential single-GPU ablations within the shared budget, preserving the 200-epoch and 200-batch limits; compare only the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.
idea.pseudocode:
Initialize one GRU model per category with trainable decay rates a.
For each batch from family-specific sample_batch:
  Construct gaps from observed training-history timestamps.
  h = zeros
  For each sequence position t:
    g = bounded_log_gap(gap[t])
    retained = h * exp(-softplus(a) * g)
    proposed = GRUCell(item_emb(sequence[t]), retained)
    h = where(sequence[t] != 0, proposed, h)
    Save h as the causal position feature.
  Draw K eligible negatives per supervised position.
  p = predict_score(features, positive)
  n = predict_score(features, negatives)
  log_w = log_softmax(n, dim=negative_axis)
  loss = mean(-logsumexp(log_w + logsigmoid(p - n), negative_axis)
              + lambda * sum(softmax(n) * n.square(), negative_axis))
  Update all parameters jointly.
Evaluate using the unchanged validation protocol.
Save one selected checkpoint per category and write its matching predictor.

originality.positive: Combines established temporal recurrence and family-specific hard-negative weighting in a compact, testable GRU extension.
originality.negative: Both components are established techniques; their combination is incremental rather than a new modeling principle.

future_potential.positive: Provides a clear experimental route toward studying how intent retention interacts with top-ranked competitor discrimination.
future_potential.negative: Timestamp sparsity, repeated purchases and false negatives may limit transfer; benchmark gains remain unmeasured.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a small recurrent-state modification and a standard vectorized loss while retaining one network.
code_difficulty.negative: Timestamp alignment, padding, negative exclusions and embedded predictor consistency require careful implementation.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces ranking objectives including BPR-max that emphasize high-scoring negative competitors.
limitations: Does not establish gains for the pinned four-category Amazon evaluation or resolve stale intent explicitly.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR
contributions: Studies robust pairwise optimization under dynamic negative sampling and false-negative risk.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed temporal GRU combination or benchmark-specific improvements.

related_work.title: 2Gated-TimeGRU
contributions: Incorporates elapsed-time information into a GRU recommendation architecture.
limitations: Motivates temporal conditioning but does not validate the proposed decay equation on this task.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Explores text-based item representations for sequential recommendation.
limitations: Its Transformer backbone and pretraining procedure are outside this experiment's constraints; corpus-only GRU text integration remains a separate hypothesis.
